# Starter Story: Western/Global Solo Developer Founders at ~$5K–$20K/month (carousel candidates)

**Method note.** In October 2026, `WebFetch` failed on starterstory.com with a DNS error. Plain `curl` through the proxy worked (HTTP 200). Every Starter Story page cited below was downloaded and read in full. That includes the transcript Starter Story publishes on each episode page. Episode lists were taken from starterstory.com/sitemap.

**How to read the quotes.** Starter Story transcripts are auto-generated and have **no punctuation**, and they mis-spell product names. Examples: "Cloud Code" for Claude Code, "Superbase" for Supabase, "Verso" for Vercel, "ChipFast" for ShipFast.
- **VERBATIM (transcript)** means the words are copied exactly from the page transcript. Only punctuation and capitalisation were added.
- **[sic]** marks a spelling that is kept as the transcript has it.
- **PARAPHRASE** marks anything that is not word-for-word.

**Timestamps.** These are the chapter start times printed on the Starter Story episode page. Treat them as "the quote is in this chapter", not as the exact second. YouTube video IDs could not be extracted from the pages, so every link below is to the starterstory.com episode page. Each of those pages embeds the YouTube video.

**Revenue figures.** All revenue numbers are self-reported by the founders on Starter Story. None was independently verified.

## Q1. Which Starter Story founders around $10K/month fit (solo dev, simple product, clear tech stack)?

### Takeaway
Eight strong 2024–2026 candidates are all developers or self-taught builders working solo at about $9K–$15K/month. Six of them also have clear on-camera quotes about routine or focus:

| # | Founder | Product |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dmytro Krasun | ScreenshotOne |
| 2 | Sebastian Röhl | HabitKit |
| 3 | Jack Friks | PostBridge + Curiosity Quench |
| 4 | Ben Bozzay | Tech Lockdown |
| 5 | Fernando Pessagno | AI Carousels + ResumeMaker.Online |
| 6 | Leandro Zubrezki | Sync2Sheets |
| 7 | Rob Hallam | SuperX |
| 8 | Piotr Obidowski | Visualizee |

Andy Cloke (Data Fetcher, $23K) and Max (28 apps, $10K) are strong alternates.

### Cited Findings

#### 1. Dmytro Krasun — ScreenshotOne
- **Episode:** "How I Built It: $12K/Month Micro SaaS", dated **Nov 22, 2024** — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Revenue and model:** He says he has "280 customers making around 12 000 of monthly revenue", from subscriptions. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Product:** An API that "helps companies from small to big automate screenshots". His site is https://dmytrokrasun.com/ and the product is screenshotone.com. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Team:** Solo. Pat Walls calls him a "solopreneur making a great living coding and building his own products". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Time to build:** "It took me five months to build it and launch it." He calls the long build a mistake and says "Today I launch much much faster". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Hooks:**
  - "Two years ago I quit my job… just recently I reached the milestone of 10k MRR."
  - His first customer paid $7/month: "It felt like a million dollars."
  - Server costs are $3K–4K/month for about 2M screenshots, with a 40–60% margin.
  - Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)

#### Rejected candidates
- **Will Baker — Glowly.** $10K/mo, Aug 12, 2026. Rejected because he comes from freelance web design and growth is paid ads. He is not clearly a developer. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/the-lazy-method-how-i-build-10k-month-apps)
- **Non-coder founders in the same revenue band:** David Attias (STOPPR) and Vadim Strizheus (Vugola, "never shipped an app"). — [STOPPR](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-found-a-successful-app-made-it-1-different-and-now-make-12k-month-stoppr); [Vugola](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-m-19-and-i-built-this-11k-month-saas)

### Inferences
- **Best fits for a dev audience:** Dmytro, Sebastian, Leandro and Ben are career software engineers running simple single-purpose products. Jack is self-taught.
- **Best focus angle:** Ben (Tech Lockdown is a distraction blocker) and Jack (Curiosity Quench helps people scroll less). Both products are themselves about attention.
- **Starter Story's own data quality:** "Breakdown" pages (Visualizee, Supastarter) are marked "Estimated from public sources" and contain AI-style summaries. Prefer the video episodes, where the founder states the numbers on camera.

### Gaps
- Revenue was not cross-checked against founders' X posts or TrustMRR/Stripe screenshots, because of the tool-call budget.
- YouTube video IDs and exact-second timestamps were not extracted. Only chapter times are available.
- For Rob Hallam, it is unclear whether Thibaut is still a partner or co-owner in 2026. The Aug 2026 episode says he runs "the entire thing myself".
- Full surnames are missing for "Max" in the 28-apps episode.

## Q2. What exact tech stack does each list?

### Takeaway
Video episodes give the stack in the founder's own words, in the "Tech stack" chapter. The page's "Stack" widget is often incomplete or unrelated: Sebastian's widget shows Shopify/WooCommerce, and Rob's shows only Answerthepublic.com. Use the spoken answers below.

### Cited Findings

#### Dmytro Krasun (ScreenshotOne)
- **Spoken stack (VERBATIM transcript):** "I use TypeScript for managing headless browsers and Puppeteer library I use Go language for rate limiting managing API keys and so on I use Cloudflare for storing screenshots as an API gateway to my product… Google Search Console… Google Keyword Planner… PostHoc [sic: PostHog] Analytics… CrispChat for live chat support". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Page "Stack" widget:** Google Adwords, Google Workspace, Zapier, Trello, Crisp, Digital Ocean, Medium, Node.js. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)

#### Sebastian Röhl (HabitKit), "Tech stack" chapter at 09:22
- Flutter (cross-platform), Cursor ("my AI powered IDE"), Astro (keyword research and ASO), AppFigures, RevenueCat (subscriptions), "Waycast" [sic, likely Raycast] and 1Password. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-15k-month-mobile-app)
- **Costs:** "My biggest expense is Revenue Cat… the rest can be added up to roughly 200 or 300 per month". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-15k-month-mobile-app)

#### Jack Friks (PostBridge / Curiosity Quench)
- **Spoken stack (VERBATIM transcript):** "My tech stack is Next js mostly And for mobile apps it's React Native with Expo And I use also a boilerplate to start all my web projects called ChipFast [sic: ShipFast] from my friend Mark Liu [sic: Marc Lou] I use Superbase [sic: Supabase] for the database every time". He also uses Apple Notes, a Trello board and a work timer. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-built-a-10k-month-app-from-my-mom-s-basement)
- **Page widget:** Vercel, ChatGPT. **Costs:** About $400/month. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-built-a-10k-month-app-from-my-mom-s-basement)

#### Ben Bozzay (Tech Lockdown), "Tech stack" chapter at 11:36

### Inferences
- **Recurring 2025–26 solo-dev stack:** Next.js + Supabase/Firebase + Vercel + Stripe + PostHog. Cursor and Claude Code are increasingly named as the coding tool (Piotr, Rob, Sebastian, Diego, Max).
- **Mobile:** The recurring pattern is Flutter or React Native/Expo plus RevenueCat.
- **Spellings:** Transcript misspellings must be corrected on carousels. Correct spellings are given in brackets above.

### Gaps
- Fernando's AI provider and hosting were not stated.
- Jack's AI APIs and payments were not stated in the transcript (only Vercel and ChatGPT appear in the page widget).
- Dmytro's hosting provider was not stated on camera; the widget says DigitalOcean.

## Q3. What exact quotes about focus, deep work, routine, productivity or distraction exist?

### Takeaway
Six founders have strong verbatim routine or focus quotes:

| Founder | Quote theme |
|---|---|
| Jack Friks | Single-task timer blocks of 1–2 hours |
| Ben Bozzay | 5:30am deep-dev block before his day job |
| Fernando Pessagno | Four hours of deep work each morning, skipping stand-ups |
| Rob Hallam | An eight-hour solid night-time work block, "productivity follows happiness" |
| Dmytro Krasun | A calm morning routine with an hour of reading |
| Leandro Zubrezki | Working in "spikes" and skipping low-value tasks |

Andy Cloke has a strong "power of focus over shiny objects" quote. All quotes below are **VERBATIM (transcript)**, with punctuation added.

### Cited Findings

#### Jack Friks — "Tech stack" segment (no chapters listed on the page)
> "Every day I just start a timer and I lock in. I focus on the task, one task that I'm doing. And I do that for either one hour, 90 minutes or two hours at a time. And that's helped me a lot to build fast because when you're focused you get a lot more done."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-built-a-10k-month-app-from-my-mom-s-basement). The transcript has a doubled "timer timer", which was removed here; it is otherwise verbatim.

#### Jack Friks — "Day in the life" segment
> "Most of my days I wake up pretty early, get eight hours of sleep. I try not to sacrifice the sleep. Usually read a bit and go straight to work. Probably two to four hours focused work. Then I take lunch and then I work two to four hours again… I will stop working at dinnertime because then I can sleep better [and] I'm excited to work the next day."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-built-a-10k-month-app-from-my-mom-s-basement). The transcript reads "sleep better than I'm excited", which is a likely mis-transcription.

#### Ben Bozzay — chapter "How to build alongside a full-time job" (05:29)
> "I've formed a habit of waking up really early in the morning, prioritizing development tasks and stuff that just required more focus and attention in the morning. So I would do that between 5:30 and 8 o'clock, 8:30. And then if I worked on anything in the evening it might be more like marketing related, because I could do those kinds of tasks without having to be hyper focused and alert."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/my-side-project-makes-15k-month-quit-my-9-5)

#### Ben Bozzay — same chapter
> "I was just laser focused on: if I have any free time it's got to go towards the most meaningful stuff."

Also from this chapter: "If you have limited free time and energy you need to not dread waking up early in the morning to work on your side project." — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/my-side-project-makes-15k-month-quit-my-9-5)

Things start going even better by working less time. So I decided to stick with these four hours of deep [work] each morning. Having this constraint kind of forces you to be intentional about your to do list. You focus on what's important."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-make-15k-month-with-2-ai-apps). The transcript literally says "four hours of deep each morning"; the word "work" is implied.

#### Fernando Pessagno — same segment
> "It feels great just to skip the daily stand ups… I woke up without any alarm. My calendar is empty… this gives me also the mental clarity to focus [on] what's important on the business."

Also from this segment: "I make sure to work even on weekends. I feel that really keeps the momentum going." — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-make-15k-month-with-2-ai-apps)

> "When everything goes quiet at night and nobody's texting you… I just love going fully in on my work and that's how I get into flow state. I just like to front load the chores and hard stuff and then make it so that when I go to work later in the evening that is all I'm doing. So I can go fully a full eight hour solid work block and there's nothing else. There's nobody talking to me. That's all I'm doing."

- "I wake up 11 a.m., 12 p.m." He describes himself as a night owl who lives "the reverse typical guru advice lifestyle". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-work-22k-month-solopreneur)

> "My philosophy is you pick one stack, learn it deeply and ignore all of the noise, because too many people spend way too much time nowadays chasing new technologies instead of just shipping."

> "Do things with intention, not with emotion. Figure out what you want, cut out all of the noise and then do an insane amount of volume with intention."

#### Dmytro Krasun — routine segment
> "I wake up, I help my wife to send kids to school, to kindergarten. Then I just go home and drink a cup of coffee, or I just go to some local cafe… And I always, always, every morning I read at least one hour of some book. So then I work till the evening till the kids come."

> "If you're a solopreneur especially you need to take care of your mental health because it's your only tool that you use every day… Having a clear mind and thinking is one of the most leveraged things you can do in your business."

> "I usually work in spikes. So when I have to do development I kind of put together a lot of tasks, do a huge spike of work, and then I chill. Spike, chill. That's kind of my way of working… If I see that a task or something is not going to move the needle I just don't do it and focus my time on something else."

Context: his day starts at about 7–7:30am with breakfast and the kindergarten drop-off. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-9k-month-micro-saas)

#### Sebastian Röhl — "Advice" (11:53)
> "I couldn't find motivation to code on my own apps after I programmed for eight hours on my regular job. So quitting my job was actually the only chance to get this started… this ultimately helped me to focus on my stuff."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-15k-month-mobile-app)

#### Andy Cloke (alternate) — "The power of focus" (09:01)
> "The biggest lesson has been the power of focus over chasing shiny objects… every time I start to get distracted or I'm not working hard enough I literally go to Claude and I say 'be my business coach and make me focus on the thing that's working and talk me out of trying to launch something new.' And I'm embarrassed to say that it actually works pretty well."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-23k-month-micro-saas)

#### Piotr Obidowski — "Advice" (09:51)
Not a focus quote, but usable as a simplicity line:

> "Don't build the most powerful product you can. Build the simplest product your customer needs."

Source: [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-failed-for-700-days-before-my-app-hit-10k-month)

#### Max (alternate) — PARAPHRASE
The episode description says Max "builds apps before and after work". On camera his advice is: "Get it ready… just one single feature, ship it". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/max)

### Inferences
- **Recurring routine pattern:**
  - One protected deep-work block (morning for Ben, Fernando and Jack; night for Rob).
  - Sleep protected first (Jack, Rob).
  - Few or no meetings (Fernando's "calendar is empty").
  - Strict prioritisation of the tasks that "move the needle" (Rob, Leandro).
- **Explicit "no meetings":** Only Fernando says this directly ("skip the daily stand ups", "my calendar is empty"). None of the founders reviewed uses the terms "time blocking" or "deep work" verbatim. The closest are Fernando's "four hours of deep [work]" and Rob's "eight hour solid work block".

### Gaps
- Sebastian, Piotr and Diego do not describe a daily routine in these episodes.
- Saying no to distractions is only implicit, except for Andy's Claude-coach quote and Ben's product itself.
- No quotes were cross-checked against the founders' own X or blog posts.

## Q4. Notable carousel hooks

### Takeaway
The strongest hooks are:
- **Built fast:** "built it in two weeks" (Leandro) and "banged it out in two months" (Sebastian).
- **Quit or was let go:** quit his job (Dmytro, Sebastian), fired the day before vacation (Fernando), laid off and chose the side project (Ben).
- **Zero marketing spend:** $0 marketing (Diego, Saeed).
- **Long failure, then success:** 700 days at about $100/month before $10K (Piotr), five products that made $0 (Rob).
- **Short or unusual hours:** 4 hours a day (Fernando), and 5:30–8:30am before work (Ben).

### Cited Findings
- **Leandro:** "I built it in two weeks and it has been around for four years now" / "My app does one thing and it makes 9k a month". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-9k-month-micro-saas)
- **Sebastian:** "I kept it really simple and clean and just banged it out in two months". He also quit his job with "12 months of runway". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-15k-month-mobile-app)
- **Dmytro:** "Two years ago I quit my job". His first customer paid $7, and "It felt like a million dollars". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-12k-month-micro-saas)
- **Fernando:** He was fired "just a few weeks after a very positive performance review… one day before my planned vacations". He now works 4 hours a day. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-make-15k-month-with-2-ai-apps)
- **Ben:** He was laid off in 2023 and went full time on his side project. He had no logo until he had a few hundred customers. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/my-side-project-makes-15k-month-quit-my-9-5)
- **Jack:** He taught himself to code within a year and built from his mom's basement. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-built-a-10k-month-app-from-my-mom-s-basement)
- **Piotr:** "For the two first years it was a nightmare I was actually stuck at 100 per month". He built it all solo while employed full time. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/i-failed-for-700-days-before-my-app-hit-10k-month)
- **Rob:** Five products made "a whopping zero dollars" over two and a half years. He wakes at 11am and works through the night. — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/robv4); [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-work-22k-month-solopreneur)
- **Diego:** "Just by using Reddit alone I've been able to get over 1 million eyes on my product while spending 0 in marketing". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-used-reddit-to-hit-17k-mrr-with-zero-audience)
- **Saeed:** He "launched my first extension within like two or three days". "I have not done any ads". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-i-built-it-20k-month-chrome-extension)
- **Max:** "I have a record one app I've built in two hours". — [Starter Story](https://www.starterstory.com/max)

### Inferences
- **Best focus-themed carousel set:**
  - Jack (timer, one task)
  - Ben (5:30am dev block, and he sells a distraction blocker)
  - Fernando (4 hours, no stand-ups)
  - Rob (8-hour night block, "productivity follows happiness")
  - Dmytro (an hour of reading each morning, mental clarity)
  - Leandro (spike/chill, skip low-impact tasks)
  - Andy (Claude as a focus coach)
- **Best tech-stack carousel set:** Rob, Piotr, Andy and Dmytro, who give the most detailed and developer-specific stacks.

### Gaps
- Instagram reuse rights for Starter Story clips and screenshots were not checked here. See usage_rights_and_policy.md in this folder, if one exists.
